name: numerical: The Amazon e-commerce data science team fits a model…
questionText: The Amazon e-commerce data science team fits a model to gain understanding of the extent to which having an Amazon Prime membership leads customers to buy more from the platform than customers without a Prime membership. The data set includes two variables: total Sales revenue for a customer account and a dummy variable representing whether the customer had a Prime membership (0 = no, 1 = yes). The fitted model equation is: Sales=764+1323∗Prime+e What is the predicted sales revenue for a customer who is a Prime member? Round your answer to the nearest dollar.

name: multiple_choice: As an Advanced Accounting Analytics intern at Gringotts Bank,…
questionText: As an Advanced Accounting Analytics intern at Gringotts Bank, you are tasked with investigating factors that explain variation in account balances accrued by credit card holders. The credit.csv file contains a data set with information on 400 credit card account holders, including the following variables: Balance: credit card balance, i.e. debt owed to bank ($ dollars) Income: cardholder annual income ($ thousands of dollars) Limit: credit spending limit ($ dollars) Student: Yes/No indicator for whether or not the cardholder is a part-time or full-time student Fit a linear regression model for Balance in terms of the following predictors: Income Student Limit the interaction between Student and Limit Use this model to predict the account balance for a student cardholder with an annual income of $15,000 and a credit spending limit of $3,000. This amount is closest to which of the following?

name: multiple_choice: This question revisits the data on video-game reaction time…
questionText: This question revisits the data on video-game reaction time that we analyzed in class and in Lesson 14. Specifically, we'll consider three variables from this data set (two that we looked at before, and one that we didn't): PictureTarget.RT: the subject's reaction time in milliseconds when presented with a visual stimulus FarAway: a dummy variable for whether the stimulus (i.e. the “bad guy” popping up on the screen) was near (0) or far away (1) within the visual scene. SceneLetter: a letter code (b, c, d, e, or f) indicating which of five scenes the subject was presented with. (Note: the scene letters start at b; there is no scene a in this data set) Consider the following model and its corresponding regression table: lm(PictureTarget.RT ~ FarAway + SceneLetter + FarAway:SceneLetter, data=rxntime) %>% get_regression_table() %>% select(-std_error, - statistic, - p_value) Based on this regression table, which of the following statements is accurate? (1) This model includes an interaction term for the FarAway and SceneLetter variables. (2) The interaction of SceneLetter: d and a FarAway stimulus implies some decrease in reaction time (with 95% confidence) after accounting for the main effects. (3) If the stimulus is FarAway and the interface shows SceneLetter: a , we expect a slower reaction time by approximately 20-75 milliseconds with 95% confidence.

name: multiple_answers: Which of the following statements about interactions and /…
questionText: Which of the following statements about interactions and / or correlated predictors is accurate? Choose all correct statements.

choices.label: A
choices.text: One simple way to diagnose an interaction between a numerical predictor and a categorical predictor is to make a plot -- to visualize a separate trend line in each category and to compare their slopes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Any time two predictor variables X1 and X2 are correlated, we would expect to need an interaction between those two variables in our model.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Interaction terms are used in regression models to describe situations where the relationship between some X predictor variable and response variable Y depends on some other variable in the context.

choices.label: D
choices.text: There could be an interaction effect between two variables even if those variables are statistically independent of one another.

name: multiple_answers: In 1990, the United Nations created a single measure…
questionText: In 1990, the United Nations created a single measure that ranges between zero and one -- the Human Development Index (HDI) -- to summarize health, education, and economic status for world countries. Below is the equation for a fitted model to predict response variable HDI in terms of two predictor variables: Life expectancy and average years of School. HDI = -0.34 + (0.01 * Life) + (0.02 * School) + E Which of the following is an accurate interpretation of the coefficient for Life expectancy? Select all correct answers.

choices.label: A
choices.text: The change in HDI associated with a one-year increase in Life expectancy, holding other predictors constant.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The overall relationship between Life expectancy and HDI.

choices.label: C
choices.text: For every one-year increase in Life expectancy, we expect HDI to increase by 0.01 (irrespective of years of School).

choices.label: D
choices.text: A partial slope representing the relationship between Life expectancy and HDI, adjusting for average years of School.

name: multiple_choice: The data set in cars.csv includes information on the…
questionText: The data set in cars.csv includes information on the gas mileage of virtually every model of vehicle offered for sale to U.S. consumers during 2020. You will fit a regression model to predict city fuel economy in miles per gallon (city variable) in terms of the following predictor variables: powertrain -- vehicle powertrain type: Diesel, EV, FFV, Gasoline, Hybrid, or Plug-in Hybrid category -- vehicle type: Car, Small Car, SUV/Van, Truck, Two-seater, or Wagon The EV level of the powertrain variable corresponds to battery EVs --- that is, electric vehicles like Teslas and Nissan Leafs. (In case you're curious, for EVs, the government reports the city variable as the "equivalent" MPG based on the vehicle's battery usage.) Which of the following statements about the powertrain: EV coefficient is accurate? (1) EVs have an average of 82.6 city miles-per-gallon (equivalent). (2) EVs have an average that is 82.6 city miles-per-gallon (equivalent) higher than that of vehicles with a Diesel Powertrain. (3) EVs have an average of 102.8 city miles-per-gallon (equivalent).

name: numerical: Next semester, your work-study position involves data science support…
questionText: Next semester, your work-study position involves data science support for a visiting scholar interested in dragon demography. You are working with the dragons.csv file, a data frame on 2000 magnificent beasts randomly sampled from the extensive Care of Magical Creatures database including the following variables: lifespan -- age of dragon in years color -- color of dragon (black, blue, green, red) spikes -- indicator for spikes on body or tail (spikes, without) lost_teeth -- number of lost teeth scars -- number of scars height -- in yards weight -- in tons Fit a linear model regressing height on two predictors: weight and color. Calculate model fit statistics. What is the typical error that we expect in using this model to predict height? Enter your numerical answer rounded to two digits.

name: matching: The georgia.csv file contains Georgia’s county-level voting data from…
questionText: The georgia.csv file contains Georgia’s county-level voting data from the 2000 presidential election. The 2000 election was among the most controversial in history; it turned on an esoteric set of issues surrounding voting machines and vote counts, and wasn't finally resolved until the Supreme Court's ruling in Bush v. Gore. For our purposes, the relevant variables are: votes: number of votes recorded ballots: number of ballots cast equipment: indicator for whether county used Optical scan voting machines or else Other equipment urban: indicator for whether county is predominantly Urban or Rural based on population density Use the mutate() function to define a new variable called ucountPct: measuring the percentage of ballots in a county that were "undercounted" or "spoiled", (i.e., ballots cast where no legal vote was recorded because the machine could not read the vote). Was there a difference, on average, in undercount percentages between Urban counties versus Rural counties? Use these variables, along with a large-sample 95% confidence interval, to evaluate the following statements:

blanks.label: In the sample, the undercount rate was higher in Rural counties.
The difference in means is not statistically significant with 95% confidence.
With 95% confidence, the undercount rate is at most around 2% lower in Urban counties.
In the sample, the undercount rate was higher in Urban counties.
The difference in means is statistically significant with 95% confidence.

name: multiple_choice: Why do we need a control group in experimental…
questionText: Why do we need a control group in experimental design? Identify the accurate statements below. (1) To rule out natural change and variation (as distinct from change related to some experimental treatment) as an explanation for the outcomes we observe. (2) To rule out alternative explanations for the outcome of the experiment related to placebo effects. (3) To provide a basis for comparison for those who received the treatment.

name: multiple_choice: A tech journalist blogged recently about a perceived lack…
questionText: A tech journalist blogged recently about a perceived lack of female founders in the latest batch of startups accepted to the Hooli Hive accelerator, operated by one of the world’s leading digital technology platforms. Recent industry statistics indicate that 33% of US tech startups have at least one female founder. Of the 75 founding teams admitted to the Hooli Hive accelerator, only 16 included a female founder. Is this seemingly low proportion of females an indication of gender bias at Hooli? On the other hand, could this observation simply be the result of natural sampling variability in founding team demographics? name: multiple_answers: Which of the following is true of the t…
questionText: Which of the following is true of the t distribution? Select all correct answers.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use of the t-distribution does not assume that we know the population standard deviation sigma (σ).

choices.label: B
choices.text: When we use an estimate of sigma (σ) rather than the true σ (as assumed with de Moivre’s equation), it introduces in our calculation an extra source of uncertainty for which the t-distribution attempts to compensate.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The RStudio function t.test() is based on this distribution.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Calculating a confidence interval based on the t-distribution is effectively computing a confidence interval based on the Central Limit Theorem and de Moivre’s equation, with a minor correction that widens the interval to account for small sample sizes.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The t distribution is unimodal and symmetric, similar to the normal distribution.

name: multiple_answers: The data science team at Florean Fortescue's Ice-Cream Parlour…
questionText: The data science team at Florean Fortescue's Ice-Cream Parlour is interested in how weather might impact sales. Over a period of a few months, they collect data on the quantity of ice cream orders during specific time frames as well as the outside temperature during that time frame. Their goal is to use a statistical model to understand how changes in temperature predict changes in consumer demand for ice cream, as measured by quantity of orders sold. Which of the following statements accurately describe such a model? Select all correct answers.

choices.label: A

choices.label: B

choices.label: C
choices.text: Quantity sold should be the response Y variable, and temperature should be the predictor X variable.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Quantity sold should be the predictor X variable, and temperature should be the response Y variable.

name: numerical: Contract bridge, or simply bridge, is a trick-taking card…
questionText: Contract bridge, or simply bridge, is a trick-taking card game using a standard 52-card deck. One of the world's most popular card games, it is played by four players in two competing partnerships, with partners sitting opposite each other around a table. Imagine that you are president of the Bevo Bridge Club. It is your duty to organize game gatherings each week. One regular concern is whether or not an even table split will turn up to play. There are 15 club members. You need either 4 or 8 or 12 players in order to have the right split for tables. Over time, you have observed that a 70% probability that any given club member will attend any given gathering. Assuming that members attend independently of each other, what is the probability that exactly 4 players OR exactly 8 players OR exactly 12 players will show up for the next gathering? Enter your answer as a decimal rounded to three digits.
